aria: Animated recap of the Lakers' 131 to 123 road win over the Suns: Quentin Grimes' pull-up 3-pointer off the glass with 32.2 seconds left that made it 129 to 121, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Luka Dončić's 43 points and 9 assists, the top scorers, how the Lakers won, and the next game against Charlotte.
notes: Box score from the Lakers' 131–123 win over the Phoenix Suns at Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix on Nov 15, 2026, from the SI.com box score and play-by-play, with game details from the Associated Press (via ABC7 and CBS News Los Angeles), the Los Angeles Times and the New York Post (both via Yahoo Sports), Yahoo Sports, Bright Side of the Sun (via Yahoo) and Bleacher Report. All 131 Los Angeles points and all 123 Phoenix points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: 33–24 after one, 64–54 Lakers at the half, 104–80 after three. Team totals (field goals 43 of 86 to 43 of 92, threes 16 of 41 to 13 of 46, free throws 29 of 36 to 24 of 30, steals 11–4, blocks 8–3) are summed from the box score's player lines, and the IBTimes and Bright Side of the Sun recaps give the same field goals, threes and steals. Phoenix's 78 bench points are from Yahoo Sports; the Lakers' 28 are Sexton, Ziaire Williams, Mamukelashvili and Vanderbilt in the box score. The Lakers' 31-point lead came at 101–70 late in the third quarter on a Collin Sexton layup (SI.com play-by-play; Los Angeles Times). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Sunday's games.

Phoenix outscored the Lakers 43–27 in the fourth and went on a 15–1 run from 116–96 to 117–111; Collin Gillespie's driving layup with 1:05 left made it 126–121, the closest the Suns got (AP; Yahoo Sports; SI.com play-by-play). Luka Dončić scored 20 in the first quarter (Los Angeles Times) and 43 on 13 of 28 shooting with 9 assists (SI.com box score); Quentin Grimes' five 3-pointers were a season high (New York Post). Devin Booker had 17 and did not play the fourth quarter (AP). Austin Reaves sat out with a bruised left heel (Los Angeles Times; AP). It was the Lakers' eighth straight win (AP; Yahoo Sports). The Lakers host Charlotte on Tuesday, Nov 17 (AP; Los Angeles Times).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Quentin Grimes' 3-pointer with 32.2 seconds left that made it 129–121 (the Los Angeles Times and the New York Post give 32.2 seconds, AP 34 seconds; the SI.com play-by-play logs it as a pull-up bank three, assisted by Dončić, with the score going from 126–121 to 129–121). The New York Post describes Grimes crashing the offensive glass after a missed corner three before he banked in the pull-up. It is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Los Angeles Lakers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Grimes' listed 6-foot-5 and 207 pounds (Wikipedia), with his arms scaled to the 6-foot-8 wingspan measured at the 2021 NBA Draft Combine (NBADraft.net), in the Lakers' road purple with No. 5 (Wikipedia). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
